failures.reason: The expectation assumed only the emitter calls E918 after the setup. The trace showed five E918 calls by code at 109E4 (three) and 10A00 (two) for the object at FFFF32C2, outside the pool, just after the object loops of frames 634, 797, 850, 1000 and 1053. They are now an explicit per-loop count that native applies with its own E918 recurrence before the loop; the state is never re-seeded.

The second run differed only in the setup line: the expectation listed 7DB8's CB9A row clear among the world's requests, while the transport prints it with 7DB8's selection. All 432 loop lines already matched.

The first form compared each slot's next-loop entry with the previous frame end and failed at slot 67 after 852: a lower slot's walk (the copy's 7AD6 at 853) changes it earlier in the same loop. It now compares each entry with the previous frame end except for slots another walk of that loop changed before their own walk, and each frame end with the walk exit except for slots changed after it.
The test decoder first nested each object's fields inside the event tuple; its assertions expect flat tuples, so the decoder now flattens them.

The first definitive capture (run-h4f_f2wy, with release/sanitize fixtures run-c2scn8lc and run-1u5woe6z) matched all fifteen comparisons; it was superseded only to correct three docstrings of tools/genesis_world_pool.py, whose hash the capture records.
